genxml.title: Adaptec AIC-7880 SCSI controller on the O2: host DMA and SCB register contract
genxml.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book (sibling, applied to AIC-7880)
genxml.doc: The O2 onboard SCSI controller's host-DMA window, its DMA control and FIFO status registers, the SCB page pointer, byte counter and window, and the SCSI bus signal, transfer-control and PIO registers. Offsets and widths come from the cited Adaptec AIC-7870 data book, applied to the AIC-7880 as its sibling. Every item is inferred until an AIC-7880 book or a measurement settles it.

struct.name: SCSISEQ
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 72-73 (printed 4-3 and 4-4); sibling
struct.doc: SCSI sequence control. Each bit enables one hardware selection or reselection sequence, or drives SCSI RESET#. A SCSI bus reset clears every bit except SCSIRSTO. The register reads back, so software can set and clear bits without a scratch copy.

struct.name: SXFRCTL0
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 74-75 (printed 4-5 and 4-6); sibling
struct.doc: SCSI transfer control 0, the first of two transfer-control registers. Bits 5 and 0 are not used and read zero. The two self-clearing controls, CLRSTCNT and CLRCHN, read back as zero. The reset value is not stated in the cited pages.

struct.name: SXFRCTL1
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 75-76 (printed 4-6 and 4-7); sibling
struct.doc: SCSI transfer control 1. Holds the bit-bucket and wrap controls, the parity check enable, the selection timer and its interval, active negation and the termination power enable. Every bit reads zero after reset.

struct.name: SCSISIG
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 77-78 (printed 4-8 and 4.9); sibling
struct.doc: SCSI control signals. The read side returns the state of the bus control signals. The write side sets the initiator output levels, and its three upper bits are the phase the chip expects on the next REQ pulse. The two sides share one offset and the same bit positions. Every write-side bit is cleared by chip reset, by a SCSI bus reset and by Bus Free. The read side has no reset value in the cited pages. The book's own register description gives the read side as a stale copy of the bus, which reads as the bus state.

struct.name: SCSIRATE
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 79 and 97; sibling
struct.doc: SCSI rate control for DATA. Wide DATA needs this register's WIDEXFER bit and the SBLKCTL SELWIDE bit both set. The sibling's page shows every bit of the register resetting to zero. Bits 6 to 4 select the synchronous transfer rate. Read-back is not stated.

struct.name: SCSIID
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 80; sibling
struct.doc: Target ID in bits 7:4 and own ID in bits 3:0. Both are four-bit fields, so the sibling addresses IDs 0 to 15 on the wide connection. Chip and PCI reset clear both nibbles. The own ID is the initiator's address during Selection Out. Public drivers commonly write own ID 7 after reset. That is software configuration, not a reset value.

struct.name: SCSIDATL
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 81 (printed 4-12); sibling
struct.doc: SCSI data latch used for automatic and manual PIO, one byte per access. The book says an access drives the SCSI ACK (as initiator) or REQ (as target) active as it happens. The value after chip reset is unknown, and valid data loads after the first REQ and ACK. The high byte in 16-bit mode is a separate register and is not described here.

struct.name: CLRSINT1
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 78 and 86; sibling; Linux aic7xxx.reg (db2ddb87143519e20a95aa36c60b36107b736a58)
struct.doc: Write-only SCSI interrupt clears. Only CLRATNO, bit 6, is listed here; the bit positions of the other clears (CLRREQINIT, CLRPHASECHG, CLRBUSFREE) are not in the cited extract. Writing one to CLRATNO clears the initiator ATN output set through SCSISIGO. Read-back is not stated.

struct.name: SIMODE0
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 91 (printed 4-22); sibling
struct.doc: SCSI interrupt mask 0. Setting a bit enables the matching SSTAT0 status to assert the SCSI interrupt. Only the bit this unit uses is listed here.

struct.name: SIMODE1
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 92 (printed 4-23); sibling
struct.doc: SCSI interrupt mask 1. Each set bit lets the matching SSTAT1 status assert SCSIINT on IRQA#.

struct.name: SCSIBUSL
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 93 (printed 4-24); sibling
struct.doc: SCSI data bus, read directly. The book says the data is gated from the bus to the internal data bus and is not latched in the SCSI module. A read therefore sees the byte on the bus without taking the latch. Nothing in the cited pages says it acknowledges the byte, and the book ties the ACK drive to SCSIDATL accesses, so this read is taken not to acknowledge (inferred from the book's wording, not stated).

struct.name: SHADDR
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 58-59 and 93 (printed 4-24); sibling
struct.doc: SCSI-side host address, four bytes at 0x14 to 0x17, least significant byte first, so byte n holds address bits 8n+7 to 8n. Loaded when the host address at 0x88 to 0x8b is written and HADDLDSEL is 0. Counts up while STCNT counts down. Saved by the Save Data Pointers message. Zero after reset.

struct.name: SELID
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 59 and 95 (printed 4-26); sibling
struct.doc: Selection and reselection ID. Holds the ID of the device that selected or reselected this controller on the last such phase.

struct.name: SBLKCTL
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 80 and 96-97; sibling
struct.doc: Block control. The SELWIDE bit selects the physical SCSI connection width. Its reset value follows the wide-select pin WIDEPS# sampled at reset, and the O2's strap state is unknown, so the register has no reset value here. Bits 7 and 6 reset to one, bit 5 resets to zero, and bits 4, 3, 2 and 0 read zero.

struct.name: SEQCTL
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 98 (printed 4-29); sibling
struct.doc: Sequencer control. Bit 4 selects the sequencer clock divider, bit 2 requests one single step, bit 1 resets the sequencer RAM address pointer and bit 0 gives the host access to sequencer RAM. Bit 6 disables the host pause request. Bits 7, 5 and 3 (PERRORDIS, FAILDIS and BRKADRINTEN) are in the book but are not described on this unit. The reset value is the one the book's bit table gives in parentheses, not a value read after initialisation.

struct.name: SEQADDR0
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 99 (printed 4-30); sibling
struct.doc: Low eight bits of the sequencer RAM address that executes on the next clock edge. The driver writes it while the sequencer is paused to change where execution resumes, and uses it as the start address when loading sequencer RAM. While loading, the address steps up after every fourth byte. A write to SEQADDR[1:0] clears that byte index. RST# and CHIPRST clear the address to zero.

struct.name: SEQADDR1
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 99 (printed 4-30); sibling
struct.doc: Bit 0 is bit 8 of the sequencer RAM address, which covers the 512 instruction words. Bits 7 to 1 are reserved in the book, and their read-back is not stated. RST# and CHIPRST clear the register.

struct.name: ACCUM
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 60 and 100 (printed 4-31); sibling
struct.doc: Accumulator: temporary holding place for sequencer ALU operations.

struct.name: SINDEX
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 60 and 100; sibling
struct.doc: Source index: a temporary value, or the address that the sequencer's indirect source port SINDIR reads. The sequencer increments it after each indirect transfer.

struct.name: DINDEX
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 60 and 101; sibling
struct.doc: Destination index: a temporary value, or the address that the sequencer's indirect destination port DINDIR writes. The sequencer increments it after each indirect transfer.

struct.name: BRKADDR0
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 60 and 101; sibling
struct.doc: Low eight bits of the sequencer breakpoint address. Cleared to zero by reset.

struct.name: BRKADDR1
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 60 and 102 (printed 4-33); sibling
struct.doc: Breakpoint disable and the top address bit. Reset to 0x80, which leaves the breakpoint disabled.

struct.name: ALLONES
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 102 (printed 4-33); sibling
struct.doc: Read-only port that returns 0xff to the host and to the sequencer. It is a source for logical and arithmetic functions. The book gives no write function, so a write is outside the published interface and its effect stays unknown.

struct.name: ALLZEROS
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 102-103 (printed 4-33 to 4-34); sibling
struct.doc: Read returns 0x00 and does not return an earlier write. Written as the destination NONE, the byte is discarded and no location changes. Both directions share the offset, so the write side is described here rather than as a separate register.

struct.name: FLAGS
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 103 (printed 4-34); sibling
struct.doc: Sequencer flags, read only.

struct.name: SINDIR
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 103 (printed 4-34); sibling
struct.doc: Sequencer-only indirect source port. A read returns the byte SINDEX addresses, then SINDEX increments. The host cannot reach this port.

struct.name: DINDIR
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 104 (printed 4-35); sibling
struct.doc: Sequencer-only indirect destination port. A write stores the byte at the address DINDEX holds, then DINDEX increments. The host cannot reach this port.

struct.name: FUNCTION1
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 104 (printed 4-35); sibling
struct.doc: A write stores the byte. Bits 6:4 form an octal value, and a read returns the one-hot byte with bit N set, where N is that value. The book does not define the meaning of bits 7 and 3:0, whether a write keeps them, or the reset value. Those stay unknown.

struct.name: STACK
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 60 (printed 3-6) and 105 (printed 4-36); sibling
struct.doc: Read-only return-stack port. Four return entries, newest first, are read one byte at a time: the low byte of an entry, then its high byte, which carries the high address bit. Each high-byte read advances the read pointer to the next entry, so eight byte reads bring the pointer back to its start. The read value after initialisation is zero. The reset values of the individual backing words are not specified in the cited pages. The book gives no write function, so a write is outside the published interface and its effect stays unknown.

struct.name: DSPCISTATUS
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 61 and 136 (printed 4-67); sibling
struct.doc: Data FIFO threshold select, with a read-only view of six PCI status bits. Power-on reset forces the threshold select to zero. Writes change only bits 7 and 6.

struct.name: HCNTRL
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 61 and 137-138 (printed 4-68 and 4-69); sibling
struct.doc: Host control. RST# or a CHIPRST write sets it to 0x05: the sequencer is requested paused and chip reset is acknowledged. A write that changes PAUSE is not complete until a read returns the written value.

struct.name: LHADDR
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 139-140 (printed 4-70 to 4-71); sibling
struct.doc: Host PCI address for the host DMA transfer, four byte registers at 0x88 to 0x8b. Loading it also loads SHADDR. The byte significance across the four bytes is not in the cited extract and stays unknown. Read-back is not stated.

struct.name: HCNT
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 139-140 (printed 4-70 to 4-71); sibling
struct.doc: 24-bit host transfer count in three byte registers at 0x8c to 0x8e. A zero count inhibits host PCI requests. Loading a nonzero count clears HDONE. The byte significance across the three bytes is not in the cited extract and stays unknown. Read-back is not stated.

struct.name: SCBPTR
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 53, 63-64, 153 and 180; sibling
struct.doc: SCB page select latch. All eight bits read back as written, whether or not external SRAM is selected and however much of it is fitted, so a read-back of 0xff does not show that page 255 exists. Selects one 32-byte page for the SCB window and for SCBCNT-addressed accesses. Reset is zero as the cited book's reset description gives it, not a value read after initialisation.

struct.name: INTSTAT
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 141-142 (printed 4-72 and 4-73); sibling
struct.doc: Interrupt status. The sequencer writes these causes, and the host reads them without pausing the sequencer. SEQINT, SCSIINT and BRKADRINT pause the sequencer at once; CMDCMPLT does not. Bits 3 to 0 clear individually through CLRINT.

struct.name: CLRINT
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 143-144 (printed 4-74 and 4-75); sibling
struct.doc: Clear interrupt, the write side of offset 0x92. A one written to a bit clears the matching INTSTAT cause; the bits self-clear, and the sequencer cannot write this register. The read side at the same offset is the ERROR register, whose causes (PCIERRSTAT, MPARERR, DPARERR, SQPARERR, ILLOPCODE) are described in the prose page.

struct.name: DFCNTRL
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 139, 145-148 (printed 4-70, 4-76 to 4-79); sibling
struct.doc: Data FIFO control. Bits 5 and 4 enable SCSI and SCSI-block DMA, bit 3 enables host DMA, bit 2 selects the direction, bit 1 flushes the FIFO and bit 0 resets it and self-clears. Cleared by PCI RST# and by the chip reset in HCNTRL. Read-back is not stated. The reset value is the cleared state the chip reset produces, not a value read after initialisation.

struct.name: DFSTATUS
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 145-148 (printed 4-76 to 4-79); sibling
struct.doc: Data FIFO status. Reports FIFOEMP, FIFOFULL, FIFOQWDEMP, MREQPEND and HDONE. Only DFTHRSH, bit 2, has a listed position here; the other bit positions are not in the cited extract and stay unknown. MREQPEND is a pending need, not a PCI request in flight.

struct.name: DFDAT
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 63; sibling
struct.doc: Data FIFO port, one byte per access. A read takes one valid byte from the FIFO and a write supplies one. The book gives no reset value (init xx).

struct.name: SCBCNT
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 63-64, 153-154, 176-177 and 180; sibling
struct.doc: SCB byte counter. Bits 6:5 read zero. With SCBAUTO clear the window offset selects the byte and the counter is not used. With SCBAUTO set the counter replaces the window offset, advances once per completed logical SCB byte access and wraps within the 32-byte page. Reset is zero as the cited book's reset description gives it.

struct.name: QINFIFO
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 69 (layout), p. 63 (lists it at M98, which the layout does not match); sibling
struct.doc: Queue-in FIFO. The host writes SCB IDs and the sequencer removes them. The address follows the SCB device-register layout on PDF p. 69; the register table on PDF p. 63 prints it as 0x98.

struct.name: QINCNT
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 63 and 69; sibling
struct.doc: Queue-in count: entries waiting in the queue-in FIFO. Zero when empty.

struct.name: QOUTCNT
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF p. 61; sibling
struct.doc: Queue-out count, read by the host only. Zero when empty.

struct.name: SCBWIN
struct.from: Adaptec AIC-7870 Data Book, PDF pp. 63-64, 153-154 and 176-177; sibling
struct.doc: SCB window: 32 byte positions of the page that SCBPTR selects. Sequencer accesses are byte wide. Host reads are byte wide. Host writes are byte wide in either SCBAUTO mode, and a full four-byte write is accepted only with SCBAUTO set, filling four successive positions. Host access needs a paused sequencer or the automatic access pause. Byte order of the four data bytes against the CPU is not in the cited extract and stays unknown.
